answer: Forced trajectory divergence. Each identity gets a basalt-seeded random branch schedule and must commit a trajectory hash after every step. A vine records these commits; duplicate hashes across identities are rejected because exact clones cannot diverge. The system also assigns a challenge route tagged violet that forks on local state, so copied agents repeat the same fork. To pass, an attacker must train and run a separate policy per identity, paying one fresh model checkpoint plus per-step inference per identity.
